skill.description: Guides AI agents to build Avalonia UI applications with Zafiro, ReactiveUI, DynamicData, and functional MVVM conventions.
skill.summary: Apply Zafiro-first Avalonia patterns for maintainable reactive MVVM applications.
skill.author: sickn33

The backticks on line 13 are Markdown formatting around the C# Result type. There is no shell command, Ruby execution, or user-controlled command string.
The backticks on line 23 format the term RefreshableCollection inside a guide link. This is documentation text, not shell execution.

content.value_statement: Avalonia projects can drift into inconsistent reactive patterns and leaky ViewModels. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward Zafiro-first MVVM conventions.
actual_capabilities: Guides Avalonia UI work toward strict MVVM separation.
Promotes Zafiro helpers before custom reactive logic.
Defines DynamicData operator preferences for collection pipelines.
Documents naming, error handling, and field style conventions.
Provides patterns for validation, refreshable collections, and error notifications.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run project analysis automatically.
It assumes the project already uses Avalonia, Zafiro, ReactiveUI, and DynamicData.
It does not replace framework documentation or project-specific architecture decisions.
It may need adaptation for teams with different naming rules.

use_cases.title: Implement Reactive ViewModels
use_cases.description: Create ViewModels that keep Avalonia types out of business logic and use clear reactive pipelines.

use_cases.title: Review Zafiro Usage
use_cases.description: Check whether new code uses existing Zafiro helpers before adding custom extensions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Code
use_cases.description: Align naming, validation, and error handling across a shared cross-platform UI codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Start a ViewModel
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Avalonia ViewModel for this feature using strict MVVM, Zafiro helpers, and functional error handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for new feature code

prompt_templates.title: Review Reactive Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Avalonia reactive code against the Zafiro and DynamicData rules. List concrete fixes and explain each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Collection Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this collection workflow to use DynamicData operators, lifecycle disposal, and Zafiro validation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Architecture Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose an architecture plan for this Avalonia feature using inward dependencies, immutable models, and reusable Zafiro extensions.

output_examples.input: Review a ViewModel that directly references Avalonia controls.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the MVVM violation, suggests moving UI types to the view layer, and proposes binding-based alternatives.

output_examples.input: Plan validation for a dynamic list of form stages.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a DynamicData validation pipeline, lifecycle disposal, and a user-facing error path.

output_examples.input: Compare a custom Rx helper with Zafiro shortcuts.
output_examples.output: The response maps verbose observable patterns to existing Zafiro methods and flags redundant helper code.

best_practices: Search for existing Zafiro helpers before writing custom reactive code.
Keep ViewModels free from Avalonia UI types and code-behind logic.
Use DynamicData operators for collection flows and dispose subscriptions clearly.
anti_patterns: Placing business logic inside Subscribe handlers.
Creating local SourceList or SourceCache instances for small problems.
Using exceptions for expected flow control across architecture boundaries.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for Avalonia UI applications that use Zafiro, ReactiveUI, DynamicData, and MVVM.

faq.question: Does it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: It guides code generation and review, but project requirements still define the final implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with validation logic?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Zafiro validation patterns for dynamic collections and form state.

faq.question: Does it allow Avalonia types in ViewModels?
faq.answer: No. The guidance keeps ViewModels independent from Avalonia UI types.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is Markdown guidance and does not define command execution steps.
